messages:
katie: Kickoff: we need a hardened pattern for AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC) control-plane + dataplane. Topics: DEK lifecycle + caching, mTLS vs client certs, KMS access model (grants vs policies vs cross-account), CloudTrail/audit forwarding to SIEM, rotation playbook & incident steps. Looking for an ops checklist we can standardize for all customers.

sam: +1. From prod experience: mTLS between control-plane nodes + short-lived instance role tokens for services. KMS usage: use GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext when possible, use grants for high-QPS decrypts. Keep EncryptionContext strict. :white_check_mark:

tanya: notes on caching: in-node in-memory DEK cache with TTL 60s. Entry contains ciphertext_blob only; plaintext only in ephemeral memory during operation. Use AWS KMS Decrypt with EncryptionContext to return plaintext, then immediately encrypt DEK into local sealed secret store (node-local encrypted file or OS keystore) and zero memory. On rotation signal, publish to SNS topic to flush caches across nodes.

maria: audit logs: enable CloudTrail Data Events for kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey, plus log management calls like STS:AssumeRole and kms:CreateGrant. Ship CloudTrail to a dedicated auditing account S3 bucket with per-customer prefixes; enable S3 Object Lock (governance) for immutable retention where required. Forward events to SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) via Kinesis Firehose or EventBridge. Add a correlation_id header in control-plane requests and include that in encryptionContext to tie KMS events back to app traces.

sec-bot: Reminder: For sensitive events, include the KMS encryptionContext keys: customer_id, cluster_id, env. CloudTrail stores requestParameters which may contain EncryptionContext as a map 	2								
(verify in test infra). :warning:

sam: grants vs policies: grants recommended for hot-path because create-grant is faster and grants are enforced server-side. Use GrantConstraints to bind to EncryptionContext. Note: grants are tied to a specific CMK and will be invalidated if the key is replaced; rotate grants as part of key rotation.

katie: rotation playbook draft? planned vs compromise flows.

tanya: Planned rotation steps: 1) Create a new CMK alias e.g. alias/redwood-customer-<id>-cmk-YYYYMMDD. 2) Update key-wrapping service to prefer the new CMK for GenerateDataKey. 3) Rewrap existing DEKs: worker reads ciphertext_blob, performs KMS Decrypt (old CMK), then GenerateDataKey with new CMK and store new ciphertext_blob; mark rewrap progress. 4) Monitor and backoff if Decrypt error spikes. 5) Disable old CMK (set key state to Disabled) then schedule deletion per retention policy. For very large datasets do a rolling rewrap with idempotent checkpoints.

maria: Compromise (urgent) runbook: 1) Disable suspected CMK immediately to stop Decrypts. 2) Revoke active grants and tighten key policy to deny. 3) Create a new CMK and bootstrap it. 4) Re-encrypt/rekey DEKs (may require restore from encrypted backups). 5) Full forensic collection: export CloudTrail lines for kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey/aws:CreateGrant, collect STS AssumeRole logs, instance metadata, and relevant application logs. 6) Rotate related secrets (DB creds, tokens) if any cached plaintexts were present. 7) Notify impacted customer per SLA and compliance team. :rotating_light:

sam: example grant CLI (use constraints to limit by EncryptionContext):

```
aws kms create-grant \\
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234 \\
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-controlplane \\
  --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey \\
  --constraints '{"EncryptionContextSubset":{"customer_id":"cust-123","cluster_id":"c-1"}}'
```

katie: RBAC question: who should be able to create grants or edit key policy during rotation?

tanya: Principle: automation holds privilege. A small ops automation role (assumed by control-plane operator or CI job) should hold kms:CreateGrant, kms:ReEncrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey. Human ops accounts should be limited; require MFA and a separate approver flow to change key policy or manually disable keys. Track those manual actions in CloudTrail and require a Jira incident link.

maria: SIEM detection ideas: sudden spike in kms:Decrypt per principal > 3x baseline, Decrypts with unexpected encryptionContext values, Decrypts initiated from unusual IPs or regions, create-grant calls outside change window, and key policy changes. Correlate with failed STS attempts or new role creations. Alert severity -> runbook start.

devops-bot: infra note: update terraform module redwood_kms_key to expose grant_principals list and rotation_lifecycle variables. Add kms_audit_bucket_arn variable and enforce bucket lifecycle + object lock if required by customer.

katie: ok I will consolidate these into a draft runbook PR and include the incident checklist + playbook. Folks: anything missing, especially around in-memory caching TTLs or forensic artifacts to collect?

tanya: add one more: validation tests as part of CI - attempt Decrypt with wrong encryptionContext and ensure KMS returns AccessDenied. Also add chaos test that disables CMK to verify app fallback behavior.

maria: add quarterly audits: key policy review, grant inventory, and sample-cloudtrail checks. Also keep a retention policy for logs aligned with compliance (HIPAA/GDPR customers may need longer retention).

sam: assigning katie to produce runbook PR and tag security for review. :handshake:
